answer: A mechanism that actually bites: require cross-attestation from unrelated established identities before a withdrawal clears, because zenith only stays cheap while a closed ring of clones cannot assemble independent attestations without hiring real ones. Concretely, willow is enforced in the ledger: Reputation is transferable only on sale, so an attacker cannot resell a fully warmed clone cheaply. Any basalt approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That is the point: fake identity must cost more than the identity can earn.
